messages.content: Make the case that structured code review improves the quality of software produced by engineering teams. Address exactly these three points: (1) reviewers catch defects before release, when they are far cheaper to fix than in production; (2) reviewing each other's changes spreads knowledge of the codebase across the team and reduces reliance on single experts; (3) regular review enforces consistent coding standards that make the software easier to maintain over time. Do not address counterarguments. Write in continuous prose paragraphs only. Do not use bullet points, numbered lists, headers, bold text, or any other formatting.

message.content:
Structured code review serves as a vital practice that enhances the overall quality of software developed by engineering teams. By having peers examine proposed changes before they are integrated into the main codebase, teams are able to identify and resolve defects at an early stage, which proves significantly less expensive than addressing issues that surface only after the software has been deployed to production environments where fixes often require extensive testing, coordination, and potential downtime. 

The collaborative examination of modifications also promotes a broader understanding of the entire codebase among team members, thereby diminishing the dependency on individual experts who might otherwise become bottlenecks during development or maintenance tasks. 

In addition, the consistent application of review standards ensures that all code adheres to established conventions and practices, resulting in software that is more straightforward to maintain and evolve over extended periods as new features are added or existing ones are updated.
